structsub/capability.description: Create a structure from a written specification. Give exactly one of: `smiles` (a whole molecule), `sequence` (a peptide, 'RMA' or 'Arg-Met-Ala'), `crystal` (space group, cell and sites), `formula` (a crystal matched to a known structure type, e.g. 'NaCl'), or `zeolite` (a three-letter framework code, e.g. 'FAU'). Returns a new structure revision. Molecules are a generated conformer and peptides are not a predicted fold; relax before computing properties. For a named MOF use `open_named_framework`; to assemble a framework from nodes and linkers use `match_frameworks` then `build_framework`.
evidence: automatic: generated from the deployed route and its schema

body.description:
Where a *host* structure comes from, when it is not a file.

The counterpart to :class:`FragmentSpec`, and it exists because the two
halves of an edit had unequal footing: a fragment could be drawn, typed
as SMILES or uploaded, while the structure it was going into could only
be uploaded. Somebody with an idea and no file had nothing to open.

Exactly one source is used, tried in the order listed.

Note the difference from ``FragmentSpec.smiles``: a fragment's SMILES
*must* carry dummy atoms, because it is defined by the bonds it makes,
and a structure's must not, because a dangling attachment point in a
host is a bond to nothing.

crystal.description: A crystal from its space group, cell and sites, separated by semicolons: 'Fm-3m a=5.64; Na 0 0 0; Cl 1/2 1/2 1/2'. The cell gives only the parameters its crystal system leaves free. Options follow the sites: 'origin 1' or 'origin 2' where the group has two, 'supercell 2 2 2', or 'sphere 8 at Na' or 'block 3 3 3' to cut a finite cluster. Where the two origins give different crystals and none is stated, the specification is refused rather than guessed.
crystal.title: Crystal

formula.description: A crystal from its composition alone, matched to a known structure type: 'BaTiO3', 'MgAl2O4', 'NaCl'. The formula fixes the stoichiometry and the ion sizes, and those pick the structure type - a tolerance factor for a perovskite, a radius ratio for a rock salt - so what comes back is a plausible known type with a cell estimated by scaling that type's reference compound, NOT a predicted or measured structure. Where more than one type fits, as for the TiO2 polymorphs, the specification is refused and every candidate named - and the refusal carries them in 'choices', each with the specification that builds it, so a client can offer the choice rather than repeat the sentence. GET /build/candidates answers the same question before building. Add the type to settle it, 'TiO2 rutile' or 'BaTiO3 P4mm'. A fractional formula is a solid solution - 'La0.7Sr0.3MnO3', 'Zr0.92Y0.08O1.96' - and is built in the smallest supercell that makes its fractions whole atoms, disordered by a seeded arrangement. The same 'supercell', 'sphere' and 'block' options a crystal takes follow the formula after a semicolon. GET /build/prototypes lists the structure types.
formula.title: Formula

max_atoms.description: Largest crystal, cluster or zeolite to build, overriding the default of 5000 atoms.
max_atoms.title: Max Atoms

body.description:
Where a *host* structure comes from, when it is not a file.

The counterpart to :class:`FragmentSpec`, and it exists because the two
halves of an edit had unequal footing: a fragment could be drawn, typed
as SMILES or uploaded, while the structure it was going into could only
be uploaded. Somebody with an idea and no file had nothing to open.

Exactly one source is used, tried in the order listed.

Note the difference from ``FragmentSpec.smiles``: a fragment's SMILES
*must* carry dummy atoms, because it is defined by the bonds it makes,
and a structure's must not, because a dangling attachment point in a
host is a bond to nothing.

crystal.description: A crystal from its space group, cell and sites, separated by semicolons: 'Fm-3m a=5.64; Na 0 0 0; Cl 1/2 1/2 1/2'. The cell gives only the parameters its crystal system leaves free. Options follow the sites: 'origin 1' or 'origin 2' where the group has two, 'supercell 2 2 2', or 'sphere 8 at Na' or 'block 3 3 3' to cut a finite cluster. Where the two origins give different crystals and none is stated, the specification is refused rather than guessed.
crystal.title: Crystal

formula.description: A crystal from its composition alone, matched to a known structure type: 'BaTiO3', 'MgAl2O4', 'NaCl'. The formula fixes the stoichiometry and the ion sizes, and those pick the structure type - a tolerance factor for a perovskite, a radius ratio for a rock salt - so what comes back is a plausible known type with a cell estimated by scaling that type's reference compound, NOT a predicted or measured structure. Where more than one type fits, as for the TiO2 polymorphs, the specification is refused and every candidate named - and the refusal carries them in 'choices', each with the specification that builds it, so a client can offer the choice rather than repeat the sentence. GET /build/candidates answers the same question before building. Add the type to settle it, 'TiO2 rutile' or 'BaTiO3 P4mm'. A fractional formula is a solid solution - 'La0.7Sr0.3MnO3', 'Zr0.92Y0.08O1.96' - and is built in the smallest supercell that makes its fractions whole atoms, disordered by a seeded arrangement. The same 'supercell', 'sphere' and 'block' options a crystal takes follow the formula after a semicolon. GET /build/prototypes lists the structure types.

body.description:
Self, collective and transport diffusivity of guests, by molecular dynamics.

GCMC at ``pressure`` sets the loading and the starting configuration;
rigid guests then move in the rigid framework under the same force field,
thermostatted by stochastic velocity rescaling. The diffusivities come

atoms are placed on that cell by distance least squares so every bond
length and bond angle stays as close as it can to the structure's own;

tools.description:
Replace selected sites (whole linkers, nodes or fragments) with another fragment, for example swapping terephthalate for an amino-terephthalate linker. `selection` says which sites (as in `find_sites`), `sites` narrows to some of them, and `fragment` gives the replacement from the built-in library (`list_fragments`), an amino acid, SMILES with attachment points, or file content. The host adapts its cell by default and the result is relaxed with `relax`. Returns a new structure revision; the input revision is unchanged. The new structure is a computational model, not evidence the material can be made.
Input: `structure_revision_id` of the structure to act on. Runs as a job: the result is returned directly if it finishes within 20 s, otherwise the job is returned with status queued or running; poll calculation_get. Expensive requests (ML potentials, long runs, heavy simulations) wait for a person's approval (status awaiting_approval); do not resubmit them.

body.description: Replace selected sites with a fragment.

adapt_cell.description: Let the host adapt to the new fragment: a periodic lattice deforms, a cage opens up by moving its nodes apart.
adapt_cell.title: Adapt Cell

fragment.description:
Where a replacement fragment comes from.

Exactly one source is used, tried in the order listed: an entry from
the built-in library, an amino acid, a SMILES string, or the literal
contents of a structure file. The last is what a browser sends after a
drag-and-drop upload, and what a molecule drawn in a sketcher becomes
once exported.

Amino acids are a separate field rather than entries in ``library``
because they are a different kind of thing: twenty backbone residues
that only make sense two-connected, against a catalogue of linkers,
substituents and nodes. Merged into one list they would be two thirds
of it and drown what the catalogue is for.

isotropic_cell.description: Restrict the force-field lattice relaxation to a uniform scale. Off by default: the relaxation is anisotropic but shear-free, so the cell edges move independently and the angles do not move at all. A uniform scale cannot change the cell's shape, so on a non-cubic host the misfit ends up in the linkers instead.
isotropic_cell.title: Isotropic Cell

optimise_cell.description: Refine the lattice with the force field too. Left unset it follows the structure: on for a periodic host relaxed with scope 'all', off for a molecule or a restricted scope, where pinned atoms and a moving cell cannot both be satisfied. Set false to keep the cell that geometric adaptation produced.
optimise_cell.title: Optimise Cell
